title: Free Writing & Editing Tools
subtitle: A no-account, no-affiliate directory of free word processors, distraction-free editors, grammar help, name generators, and ebook converters.

tools.name: LibreOffice Writer
tools.description: Full-featured open-source word processor. Opens and saves .docx and .odt files, with styles, templates, and export to PDF.
steps: Download the installer from libreoffice.org.
Run the installer and follow the prompts.
Open LibreOffice Writer from your start menu or Applications folder.
Start writing; use File > Export as PDF to share.

tools.name: Apache OpenOffice Writer
tools.description: Classic open-source office suite. Writer handles documents, letters, and basic formatting without an account or subscription.
steps: Download the installer from openoffice.org.
Install and launch Apache OpenOffice.
Open Writer and begin editing your document.
Save as .odt or export as PDF when finished.

tools.name: ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors
tools.description: Free desktop office suite with strong .docx compatibility. Works fully offline; no account required for local editing.
steps: Download ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors from onlyoffice.com.
Install the app for your operating system.
Launch the Document editor and open or create a file.
Edit locally and save to your computer.

tools.name: FocusWriter
tools.description: Distraction-free writing app that hides menus and toolbars until you need them. Includes daily goals, timers, and typewriter sound effects.
steps: Download FocusWriter from gottcode.org/focuswriter.
Install and open the app.
Move your mouse to the screen edges to reveal menus when needed.
Set a daily goal or timer, then write full-screen.

tools.name: WriteMonkey
tools.description: Lightweight, portable distraction-free editor for Windows. Runs from a USB stick with no install, and asks for nothing but your words.
steps: Download the portable ZIP from writemonkey.com.
Extract the folder and run WriteMonkey.exe.
Choose a font and background in the menu, then write.
Save your file (.txt or .md) when done.

tools.name: Calmly Writer
tools.description: Minimalist in-browser editor with a focus mode that dims everything except the current paragraph. Works offline once loaded.
steps: Open calmlywriter.com in your browser.
Start typing in the blank document.
Use the menu for formatting, word count, and save options.
Save as .txt, .md, or HTML to your computer.

tools.name: Hemingway Editor (web)
tools.description: Highlights hard-to-read sentences, passive voice, and adverbs so you can make your writing bolder and clearer. The web version is free and needs no account.
steps: Go to hemingwayapp.com and paste your text.
Review the color-coded highlights (yellow = hard to read, red = very hard).
Rewrite dense sentences until the grade level drops.
Copy the polished text back into your editor.

tools.name: LanguageTool
tools.description: Open-source grammar, style, and spell checker supporting 30+ languages. The web checker works with no sign-up; desktop and plugin options are also free.
steps: Go to languagetool.org and paste your text.
Select your language and review the underlined suggestions.
Accept or ignore each suggestion as you see fit.
Optionally install the free desktop app or browser add-on.

tools.name: Slick Write
tools.description: Free web-based proofreader that checks grammar, style, flow, sentence structure, and vocabulary. Nothing to install and no account required.
steps: Open slickwrite.com in your browser.
Paste your writing into the text box.
Click Proofread and review the suggestions.
Apply the changes you like and copy the result.

tools.name: Reedsy Character Name Generator
tools.description: Generates character names by language, era, meaning, and archetype. Useful for fiction authors naming heroes, villains, and side characters.
steps: Visit the Reedsy Character Name Generator page.
Pick a category, origin, or meaning filter.
Browse the generated names and save the ones you like.
Use your favorites in your story.

tools.name: Fantasy Name Generators
tools.description: Hundreds of name generators for fantasy, sci-fi, real-world, and pet names. No account, no ads for core generation, and free to use.
steps: Go to fantasy-name-generators.com.
Choose a generator matching your setting (fantasy, sci-fi, etc.).
Click to generate a batch of names.
Pick your favorite and use it in your project.

tools.name: Calibre
tools.description: The open-source ebook library manager and converter. Converts between EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, PDF, and more, plus editing and metadata tools.
steps: Download Calibre from calibre-ebook.com.
Install and launch Calibre.
Add your book file (click Add books).
Select the book and click Convert books to choose your output format.

tools.name: Online Convert (Ebook Converter)
tools.description: Free web-based file converter that turns documents into EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, and other ebook formats. Basic conversions work with no account.
steps: Go to online-convert.com and choose Ebook converter.
Upload your document or paste a file URL.
Pick the target ebook format and start conversion.
Download the converted ebook when ready.
